note: Biallelic loss-of-function NOTCH3 mutations typically show periventricular/periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia with sparing of anterior temporal poles, whereas cysteine-altering mutations present with classic CADASIL-pattern lesions.

evidence.text: In a study of 50 patients with biallelic NOTCH3 variants, biallelic loss-of-function variants led to periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants presented with a classic CADASIL spectrum phenotype and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants ...
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

numbers.metric: patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants

evidence.text: A homozygous null NOTCH3 variant (c.2984delC) manifested with early-onset leukoencephalopathy, ataxia, and cognitive decline, displaying MRI white matter abnormalities specifically without anterior temporal pole lesions, contrasting with typical CADASIL.

source.title: Distinct neurological phenotypes associated with biallelic loss of NOTCH3 function: evidence for recessive inheritance
source.quote: WES was performed on a proband who exhibited livedo racemosa, ataxia, cognitive decline, seizures, and MRI white matter abnormalities without anterior temporal pole lesions.
